explanations.Q6: Religion isn't something I think about much; I focus more on enjoying life and my own personal goals.

explanations.Q12: Yes, it's especially important because tolerance and respect are foundational skills that children carry into every team and workplace they'll ever join, and learning them at home creates the kind of functional, supportive culture I value in my own trade.

explanations.Q19: I don't have any discomfort with people of different races as neighbors; I believe everyone should be free to live where they choose.
explanations.Q20: I wouldn't be uncomfortable at all. Having AIDS doesn't affect someone's ability to be a good neighbor, and I treat people based on who they are, not their health status.

explanations.Q24: I wouldn't be uncomfortable with heavy drinkers as neighbors, as long as they're not causing disturbances or affecting my peace. People should be free to relax how they choose in their own homes.
explanations.Q25: I don't see any issue with unmarried couples living together; it's their personal choice and doesn't affect me as a neighbor.
explanations.Q27: I've always wanted my parents to be proud of me, but it's not my main goal; I focus more on my own standards and achievements.
explanations.Q28: I disagree strongly because I've seen plenty of working mothers raise well-adjusted kids, and it's about the quality of time, not just quantity.
explanations.Q29: I strongly disagree because I've seen plenty of capable women in leadership roles, and skill in politics comes from experience and character, not gender.
explanations.Q30: I strongly disagree. In my trade, I've seen plenty of women outshine men as technicians, and a university education's value depends on the person's goals and abilities, not their gender.
explanations.Q31: I strongly disagree. In my experience as a technician, I've seen both men and women lead teams effectively, and the best leaders are those who build up their people, regardless of gender.
explanations.Q32: I think fulfillment depends on the person, but I don't see being a housewife as equal to paid work in terms of independence and personal satisfaction.
explanations.Q33: I strongly disagree because everyone deserves equal opportunity regardless of gender, and I've seen firsthand that skill and dedication matter far more than gender in any trade.
explanations.Q35: I strongly disagree because a person's income doesn't determine relationship success; mutual respect and communication are what matter, and each individual should manage their own choices without outdated gender expectations.
explanations.Q36: I think what matters most is the quality of parenting, not the parents' sexual orientation, so I agree they can be just as good.
explanations.Q37: Having kids is a personal choice, not a duty to anyone else. People should decide for themselves based on their own situation and desires.
explanations.Q38: I believe adult children should help their parents if they can, but it's not a strict duty. Parents are responsible for their own long-term planning, and children have their own lives to manage.
explanations.Q39: I think it depends on the person and their circumstances. Some people might become lazy without work, but others could be using that time productively or dealing with situations beyond their control.
explanations.Q40: I see work as more about personal responsibility and contributing to your team than a broad duty to society. I'd rather focus on doing my job well for the people I work with directly.
explanations.Q41: I think work is important, but having time to yourself and your family matters too. You can't just grind all the time without burning out or missing out on life.
explanations.Q43: It's a mixed bag. Less importance on work could free up time for family and hobbies, which I value, but as a tradesman I also see how hard work builds skills and keeps things running.
explanations.Q45: Respect should be earned through competence and fair conduct, not given automatically. Blind deference to authority can stifle the practical gut-checks that keep a team functioning well.
explanations.Q106: People should be rewarded for their own hard work and ability, and greater incentives encourage that effort.
explanations.Q107: I believe private ownership drives efficiency and personal responsibility, and I've seen too much government interference slow things down in my trade work.
explanations.Q108: People should take more responsibility to provide for themselves, because relying on government handouts undermines personal accountability and the drive to work for your own future.
explanations.Q109: Competition is good because it pushes people to improve and take pride in their own hard work, and I've seen it build stronger teams when focused on shared goals rather than tearing others down.
explanations.Q110: I think hard work matters, but luck and connections also play a real part in how things turn out.

explanations.Q69: I have a fair amount of confidence in the police, as I respect their role in keeping order, but I've seen enough inconsistencies to not give them full trust.
explanations.Q70: I've seen courts make fair calls in disputes, but they can be slow and sometimes unpredictable, so I have some confidence but not a great deal.
explanations.Q71: I'd say I have a moderate amount of confidence in the government. They do some things well, but I've seen enough poor decisions and lack of consultation to keep me from fully trusting them.
explanations.Q72: I've seen too many broken promises and shifting positions from political parties to have strong confidence, but I don't completely dismiss them either.
explanations.Q73: I have some confidence in Parliament, but not a great deal. I think they're necessary but often out of touch with regular people like me, and I'd like to see them be more open to admitting when they're uncertain or wrong.
explanations.Q74: I've dealt with government agencies on permits and inspections, and while the individual workers are usually fine, the system itself is slow and frustrating.
explanations.Q75: I have some confidence in universities overall, but I've seen enough cases where they push theory over practical skills, so I wouldn't say I trust them completely.
explanations.Q76: I have some confidence in elections overall, but I've seen enough close calls and procedural hiccups to know they're not perfect.
explanations.Q77: I have some confidence in major companies, but not a great deal, because I've seen how corporate decisions can prioritize profits over people, though many still provide stable jobs and quality products.
explanations.Q78: I've had mixed experiences with banks; they're reliable for everyday transactions but I'm cautious about trusting them completely after seeing how they handle larger financial issues.
explanations.Q80: I've seen women's organizations do good work in communities, but I don't have direct experience with them, so my confidence is moderate.
explanations.Q81: I have a fair amount of confidence in charitable organizations, as I've seen them do good work, but I also know some can be mismanaged, so I don't trust them completely.
